experiment: loop closure, three method generations under develop-freeze-test, with a ground-truth oracle bounding what any closure method could achieve
question: at native frame rate trackability is solved (guard 0.9%) and the residual ATE is accumulation drift - can loop closure remove it?

v1_photometric.design: appearance candidates -> photometric forward-backward verification -> position-only Sim(3) pose graph
v1_photometric.diagnosis: recognition true (39/41 audited) but photometric relative poses at low parallax underestimate separation; dense closures contract the map

v2_feature_based.design: SIFT (CLAHE, contrast 0.01 - default finds ~50 keypoints on smooth mucosa) + Lowe ratio + PnP/RANSAC both directions + forward-backward + v1 alias gate; closures carry rotation AND scale terms
v2_feature_based.frozen_test: dev -4.6%, tests +16.6% / +2.9% - FAIL (commit 07be41f froze constants before tests)
v2_feature_based.diagnosis: the PnP translations are ACCURATE (c2: median closure error 5.2 mm vs 31.5 mm odometry drift at the same pairs); the harm is the newly-enabled rotation+scale closure terms (post-hoc c2 ablation, same closures translation-only: -9.2%)

v3_translation_only.design: v2 stages 1-2 frozen bit-identical; pose graph uses translation-only closure edges with per-closure parallax-aware sigmas - the combination neither v1 (biased translations) nor v2 (good translations, poisoned rotation/scale) tested
v3_translation_only.freeze: commit 07a734f, before the test data was downloaded
v3_translation_only.pre_stated_bar: both tests improve, mean >= 5%, any worsening > 2% fails
v3_translation_only.verdict: FAIL on the mean-improvement clause (1.7% < 5%); neither test worsened - v3 is the first generation that never harms, and it captures most of each sequence's oracle headroom

oracle.design: replace each verified closure's measured relative pose with the GROUND-TRUTH relative position (tight sigma) and re-optimize: the upper bound of any closure measurement at the revisits this withdrawal actually contains. GT used only in this diagnostic, never in stages 1-3.
oracle.finding: even PERFECT closures recover at most 5-14% of ATE, and on one withdrawal nothing: a screening withdrawal is topologically a line - the camera sees most wall exactly once, drift accumulates where no revisit exists, and no closure constraint can correct it

conclusion: screening-withdrawal drift is NOT a loop-closure problem. The residual ~100 mm ATE at native rate needs better odometry or deliberate re-inspection maneuvers (which create the loops that closure could then exploit). The native-rate framing 'residual error is drift, the loop-closure problem' is corrected accordingly everywhere it appears.
replication_bonus: the two v3 test withdrawals extend the stride-3 frame-rate family to n=5: c1_t2 ATE 116.5 mm / 9227 mm path, 0.74x baseline, guard 4.2%; c2_t2 ATE 107.6 mm / 7493 mm, 0.84x baseline, guard 2.7%
